contradictions: Licensing jurisdiction is claimed inconsistently across sources: Anjouan is the most frequently and most directly cited (including in a brand-specific news article), but PAGCOR (Philippines), a historical/superseded Curaçao licence (via predecessor Rabidi N.V., since revoked), and a single unverifiable Costa Rica claim also appear — consistent with a pattern of regulatory-arbitrage/licence-shopping documented for this operator lineage.

The operating legal entity has changed hands multiple times within roughly 12 months per industry-watchdog reporting: Rabidi N.V. (Curaçao licence revoked, bankrupt mid-2024) -> Adonio N.V. -> Liernin Enterprises Ltd -> NovaForge Ltd (current, per most sources this session). A separate line of secondary sources found in a related prior investigation instead links the BillyBets brand to a 'Boomerang Partners'/Soft2Bet-linked affiliate network — this alternate attribution could not be reconciled with the NovaForge/Rabidi lineage and both are reported here as unresolved leads.

The target domain is branded 'billybetsportugal.com' (nominally suggesting a Portugal-focused mirror) yet independent Spanish media report the same BillyBets brand specifically targeting and gaining traction with Spanish bettors — consistent with the known industry pattern of country-named mirror domains being used to reach players outside, or in addition to, their nominal target market.

No DGOJ (Spain) authorisation was found for BillyBets or any candidate operating entity, corroborated by a brand-specific news source, while the current best-attested operator (NovaForge Ltd) and its predecessor entities are independently reported by watchdog sources as unlicensed/illegal-casino operators in a broader sense.
analystNotes: This investigation was significantly constrained by a tool-level failure: the WebFetch capability returned HTTP 403 for every URL attempted in this session, including the target site (billybetsportugal.com), the Anjouan Gaming public licence register, the FinTelegram NovaForge report and Rabidi PDF, and the Diario Avanza news article — indicating a systemic block on direct page retrieval rather than site-specific blocking. As a result, no page content (footer, T&Cs, licensing page, WHOIS record, or full article/report text) could be directly read or quoted; all findings are derived from WebSearch result snippets and AI-generated summaries of those snippets, which can occasionally over-generalise. Despite this, the investigation reached a materially stronger result than a purely inconclusive one: (1) a Spanish-language, brand-specific news article directly confirms BillyBets has no DGOJ licence and is not authorised in Spain, giving high confidence to the core enforcement question; (2) three independent industry sources converge on 'NovaForge Ltd' (Marshall Islands) as the current operator, with a well-documented corporate lineage (Rabidi N.V. -> Adonio N.V. -> Liernin Enterprises Ltd -> NovaForge Ltd) tied to a revoked Curaçao licence and bankruptcy — a solid investigative lead even though it is not yet primary-source verified. Recommend the enforcement team, from a non-blocked network path: (a) directly retrieve billybetsportugal.com's Terms & Conditions/Imprint to identify the disclosed operating company; (b) query the Anjouan Gaming public register (anjouangaming.com/public-register/) for 'BillyBets', 'NovaForge Ltd', and 'Liernin Enterprises Ltd'; (c) run a formal WHOIS query on billybetsportugal.com and its known aliases; (d) obtain the FinTelegram Rabidi Report PDF directly to corroborate the corporate-succession chain; (e) confirm the absence of a DGOJ entry via the regulator's own public operator list rather than secondary reporting alone.
